findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for users who receive a topic email without ever having visited/interacted with the topic (e.g. category watchers notified of a new topic, or mentioned/quoted users). The next line calls tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Use a creating/upserting API such as TopicUser.change instead of assuming a row exists.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is an unauthenticated-by-token GET request
findings.body: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe immediately mutates the currently logged-in user's notification level, with no signed per-recipient token and no confirmation step. Email link scanners/prefetchers will trigger it automatically, anyone the email is forwarded to who is logged in will change their own settings instead of the recipient's, and an attacker can embed the (predictable, enumerable topic id) URL in an on an external page to silently downgrade/mute a logged-in victim's topic notifications (CSRF on a GET, with check_xhr skipped). Unsubscribe links should carry a signed key identifying the recipient, and/or require a non-GET confirmation.

findings.title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: Assigning notification_level and calling tu.save! skips the logic in TopicUser.change that stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, observes after-save callbacks, and publishes a MessageBus notification_level_change. Other open clients therefore keep showing the old notification state and the change is not recorded consistently with every other notification-level change in the app. Call TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.

findings.title: First click does not actually stop notifications for watching/tracking users
findings.body: If notification_level is above regular (watching or tracking), the action only downgrades it to regular, not muted. A regular user still receives mention/quote/reply notifications for the topic, so the email promise 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and the landing page text 'You will stop receiving notifications' are false after the click the email invites; the user must discover and operate the extra dropdown to finish unsubscribing.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now hard-requires unsubscribe_url for every sender
findings.body: The shared unsubscribe_link string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, and Email::MessageBuilder passes template_args to I18n.t whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true (in both body and html_part). I18n raises MissingInterpolationArgument when a key is absent, so any current or plugin mailer that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without also passing unsubscribe_url (previously a valid, working combination) will now crash while building email. Only include the per-topic sentence when unsubscribe_url is present, or supply a default in MessageBuilder.

findings.title: No test covers the new unsubscribe behaviour end-to-end
findings.body: The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url to an existing MessageBuilder fixture, but the examples still assert only the user-preferences URL and List-Unsubscribe header; nothing asserts the per-topic URL actually appears in text/HTML bodies, and there is no controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all (level transitions watching->?, regular->muted, missing TopicUser row, wrong slug redirect, logged-out user). The nil-row crash and downgrade semantics above would not be caught by the test suite.
